events.title: AHRQ terminates dozens of patient care research grants: Report
Federal agency for healthcare quality cancels $109 million in grants
Group Says AHRQ Grant Cancellations Top $131M Across 28 States
Trump administration has quietly throttled an agency devoted to the safety of American healthcare
AHRQ Grant Freeze Halts Patient Safety Research Nationwide
$131M in AHRQ grant cancellations by state
AHRQ Grant Cancellations Escalate Fears Over Future of U.S. Health Services Research

ahrq-grant-terminations.summary: Beginning July 20, 2026, reports emerged that AHRQ had terminated dozens of patient care research grants, with cancellations initially reported at $109 million and subsequently escalating to over $131 million across 28 states. The freeze has reportedly halted patient safety research nationwide and raised broader fears about the future of U.S. health services research. For the research office, this represents a significant and growing threat to funding for healthcare quality and patient safety work spanning multiple states.
ahrq-grant-terminations.title: AHRQ grant terminations

events.title: White House admits it used keywords to kill billions worth of California research grants
Inside the federal keyword lists that canceled billions in research funding

grant-termination-keywords.summary: The White House has admitted to using keyword-based lists to terminate billions of dollars' worth of California research grants, with subsequent reporting exposing the contents of these federal keyword lists. The revelations show that grant cancellations were driven by automated or list-based screening rather than case-by-case review, raising significant concerns for institutions whose funding may have been flagged by targeted terms.
grant-termination-keywords.title: Keyword-based research grant terminations

events.title: 3 dozen of Harvard's peers back its court fight against the Trump administration

harvard-funding-legal-fight.summary: As of July 27, 2026, three dozen of Harvard's peer institutions have filed to back its court fight against the Trump administration over its research funding freeze. The case remains in litigation, and the broad support signals that other universities view the outcome as consequential for the wider research community.
harvard-funding-legal-fight.title: Harvard research funding freeze and legal challenge

events.title: Rescinding Portions of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Title VI Regulations To Align With the Statutory Text and Conform to Executive Order 14281
Nondiscrimination in Federally Assisted Programs of the National Science Foundation

hhs-title-vi-rollback.summary: On July 24, 2026, HHS rescinded portions of its Title VI civil rights regulations to align with statutory text and Executive Order 14281, followed on August 4 by a related NSF nondiscrimination rule in federally assisted programs. These changes signal an evolving federal civil rights compliance landscape for grant-receiving institutions that the office should review against current policies.
hhs-title-vi-rollback.title: HHS Title VI civil rights regulation rollback

USG Policy for Stopping High-Risk Life Sciences Research

high-risk-life-sciences-policy.summary: On July 28, 2026, the U.S. Government issued a policy for stopping high-risk life sciences research. The policy currently stands as newly announced, and its implementation details and scope of application remain to be clarified. For the research office, this signals a need to review affected life sciences projects for compliance with the new federal requirements.

events.title: NIH is again terminating grants that the Trump administration dislikes
Odds of winning NIH grants plummet as new funding policy and spending delays bite
NIH Director Bhattacharya kills more health disparities grants

nih-grant-terminations.summary: Since late July 2026, NIH has resumed terminating grants disfavored by the Trump administration, with Director Bhattacharya specifically killing more health disparities grants by August 5. Meanwhile, new funding policies and spending delays have caused the odds of winning NIH grants to plummet. This signals a sustained contraction of NIH funding tied to administration priorities, putting disparities-related and other targeted research at heightened risk.
nih-grant-terminations.title: NIH grant terminations under Trump priorities

events.title: STAT+: NIH plans to block international researchers on visas from accessing key funding avenue

nih-international-researcher-funding-blo.summary: On August 7, 2026, reporting revealed that NIH plans to block international researchers on visas from accessing a key funding avenue. As this is a newly announced plan, its full scope and implementation remain unclear, but it threatens to restrict funding access for visa-holding researchers at the university.
nih-international-researcher-funding-blo.title: NIH block on international researchers accessing funding

events.title: Pentagon expands blacklist to include China's top civilian universities
US sanctions top Chinese universities and research institutes, citing national security threat
Pentagon list threatens US science edge

pentagon-university-blacklist.summary: Over late July 2026, the Pentagon expanded its blacklist to include China's top civilian universities, followed by US sanctions on leading Chinese universities and research institutes on national security grounds. By August 1, analysts were warning that the list itself threatens the US science edge, meaning our office should watch for disruptions to research collaborations and partnerships involving named Chinese institutions.

events.title: White House unveils science funding overhaul
White House Science Report Calls For Reducing University Research Funding
White House report calls for big changes to 'calcified' U.S. science system
White House Seeks to Steer Research Funding Outside Academia
White House rolls out AI funding — and signals a new era for US science
What's missing from the White House plan for the future of US science
Senate Republicans join in rebuking White House over science funding
U.S. senators push against giving political appointees control over science funding
Controversial White House plan to overhaul US science funding faces Senate opposition
Senate appropriators unveil stopgap funding bill that blocks Trump's attempt to change science funding

science-funding-overhaul.summary: In late July 2026, the White House unveiled a major science funding overhaul that called for reducing university research funding, steering money outside academia, boosting AI investment, and reforming what it termed a 'calcified' U.S. science system. The plan quickly drew bipartisan criticism, with Senate Republicans joining Democrats to rebuke the proposal and push back against giving political appointees control over science funding. As of early August, Senate appropriators had unveiled a stopgap funding bill that blocks the administration's attempt to change science funding, leaving the overhaul stalled and facing significant legislative opposition.
science-funding-overhaul.title: White House science funding overhaul
